eligibility_reason: The Brazilian Reproducibility Initiative ran new-data, preregistered multicenter replications of 56 published Brazilian experiments (MTT, RT-PCR, EPM) and reports 90 valid replications covering 45 experiments in its primary analysis. However, the paper never identifies the original articles (only anonymized codes such as EPM1, MTT4, PCR147 in Fig. 3A; the list is in Table S3 / https://osf.io/cyjsz, which are not in the source), so no entry can be coded with an original reference.
notes: Positive but unenumerable from the document itself. Each replicated unit is 'the first comparison in the article that presented a statistically significant difference between two groups' from one original article (Methods, Experiment selection), so a complete enumeration would be one row per experiment (45 in the primary analysis of the v5 XML; 47 in the v1 PDF dated April 3, 2025, whose numbers differ throughout, e.g. r = 0.76 vs 0.82, replication rates 15-45% vs 20-44%). The main text gives no author/year citation, title, journal or DOI for any original, and references.json contains none of them. Per-experiment results appear only graphically and anonymously in Fig. 3A (log ratio of means, original vs individual replications), and the per-experiment success calls (5 criteria, Table 1/2) are aggregate rates only. Coding rows would require the supplementary Table S3 / OSF materials, which are outside the provided source. Aggregate verdict, if an auditor wants one: replication rates 20-44% depending on criterion; 12/45 (27%) experiments replicated by at least half of the applicable criteria; replication type would be direct/close (preregistered protocols transcribed from the originals, labs blind to original results, adaptations allowed only of necessity). A second coder might instead choose 'excluded' (cannot be scored because originals are unidentifiable) or a single aggregate inconclusive row; I chose positive with an empty, explicitly incomplete enumeration because the document clearly reports completed replications with new data.
